### Compases
- [Ejercicios de Análisis de Compases](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/compases/analizar-compas/): Practica el análisis de compases musicales: identifica si es simple o compuesto, el número de tiempos, el tipo de subdivisión y las unidades de tiempo, subdivisión y compás. Test online gratis.
- [Construir Escala Menor Armónica con Armadura](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/escalas/construir-escala-menor-armonica-con-armadura/): Escribe primero la armadura y luego la escala menor armónica, como en clase. Ejercicio interactivo en dos pasos: armadura + escala.
- [Construir Escala Mayor con Armadura](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/escalas/construir-escala-mayor-con-armadura/): Escribe primero la armadura y luego la escala mayor, como en clase. Ejercicio interactivo en dos pasos: armadura + escala.
- [Escala Mixolidia](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/escalas/escalas-mixolidia/): Ejercicios para identificar las escalas mixolidias en el pentagrama: la escala mayor con el 7º grado rebajado. Test interactivo gratuito.
- [Test de Equivalencias de Notas: Español, Inglés y Alemán](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/equivalencias-de-notas/): Ejercicio interactivo gratis para memorizar los nombres de las notas en español, inglés y alemán. Test de 10 preguntas, incluida la trampa del Si alemán (H y B).
- [Ejercicios para Completar Compases Online con Soluciones](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/compases/completar-compas/): Ejercicios para completar compases: qué figura o silencio falta en 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8, 9/8 y 12/8, con tres niveles, corrección al momento y ficha PDF con soluciones.
- [Ejercicios para Reconocer Compases Online con Soluciones](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/compases/reconocer-compas/): Ejercicios para reconocer compases: adivina el numerador y el denominador de 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8, 9/8 y 12/8 a partir del ritmo escrito, con corrección al momento y ficha PDF con soluciones.
- [Ejercicios de Síncopas Online | Encuentra la Síncopa](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/compases/sincopa/): Ejercicio interactivo de síncopas: toca en el pentagrama la nota donde empieza la síncopa, o «no hay síncopa» si el ritmo no la tiene. Síncopa de tiempo, de parte y de compás.
- [Ejercicios de Notas a Contratiempo Online | Encuentra el Contratiempo](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/compases/contratiempo/): Ejercicio interactivo de notas a contratiempo: toca en el pentagrama la nota que está a contratiempo, o «no hay contratiempo» si el ritmo no la tiene. Contratiempo de parte y de tiempo.
- [Valor de las Figuras en Cada Compás](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/figuras/valor-de-las-figuras/): Ejercicios del valor de las figuras y silencios en 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8, 9/8 y 12/8, con puntillo y doble puntillo. Test online y ficha PDF con soluciones.
- [Ejercicios de Grupos de Valoración Especial Online con Soluciones](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/grupos-de-valoracion-especial/): Ejercicios de tresillo, dosillo, cuatrillo y seisillo: a qué figura equivale cada grupo, con tres niveles y ficha PDF con soluciones.
- [Ejercicios: ¿Qué Cadencia Es? con Partitura Online](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/cadencias/): Reconoce si una frase termina en cadencia auténtica perfecta, imperfecta, plagal, rota o en semicadencia, a partir de los dos últimos acordes escritos en clave de sol y de fa. Tres niveles.
- [Ejercicios de Tempo y Agógica](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/tempo/): Ejercicios de tempo y agógica: qué significa cada término (Largo, Allegro, accelerando, ritenuto), ordenar velocidades y reconocer de oído los cambios de tempo.
- [Ejercicios de Dinámica y Matices](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/dinamica/): Ejercicios de dinámica musical: qué significa cada matiz (pp, mp, mf, ff) y términos como crescendo o sforzando, y ordenar de piano a forte. Con ficha PDF.
- [Ejercicios de Articulación Musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/articulacion/): Test de legato, staccato, acento, tenuto y marcato: el nombre y el signo en el pentagrama, en los dos sentidos.
- [¿Qué Compás Es? Ejercicios de Compases con Grupos de Valoración Especial](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/grupos-de-valoracion-especial/que-compas-es/): Reconoce el compás de una medida llena de tresillos, dosillos, cuatrillos y seisillos, simplificando cada grupo a su figura equivalente. Tres niveles, de un grupo al compás entero.
- [Ejercicios de Comienzo Tético, Anacrúsico y Acéfalo con Soluciones](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/comienzo-tetico-anacrusico-acefalo/): Distingue el comienzo tético, anacrúsico y acéfalo de una melodía a partir de sus dos primeros compases. Tres niveles, corrección al momento y ficha PDF con soluciones.
- [Ejercicios de Final de Frase en Tiempo Fuerte y Débil con Soluciones](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/final-tiempo-fuerte-y-debil/): Distingue si una melodía termina en tiempo fuerte (íctico) o en tiempo débil (posíctico) a partir de sus dos últimos compases. Tres niveles, corrección al momento y ficha PDF con soluciones.
- [Construir la Escala Cromática](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/escalas/construir-escala-cromatica/): Escribe la escala cromática ascendente o descendente desde cualquier nota. Ejercicio interactivo gratuito: sostenidos al subir, bemoles al bajar.
- [Construir Escalas Mayores Mixtas Principales](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/escalas/construir-escala-mayor-mixta-principal/): Construye las escalas mayores mixtas principales en el pentagrama: la mayor con la 6ª rebajada (♭6) y la 2ª aumentada característica. Ejercicio interactivo gratuito.
- [Construir Escalas Mayores Mixtas Secundarias](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/escalas/construir-escala-mayor-mixta-secundaria/): Construye las escalas mayores mixtas secundarias en el pentagrama: la mayor con la 6ª y la 7ª rebajadas (♭6 ♭7). Ejercicio interactivo gratuito para colocar las 8 notas.
- [Construir Escalas Mixolidias](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/escalas/construir-escala-mixolidia/): Construye las escalas mixolidias en el pentagrama: la escala mayor con la 7ª rebajada (♭7). Ejercicio interactivo gratuito para colocar las 8 notas.
- [Construir Escalas Menores Naturales](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/escalas/construir-escala-menor-natural/): Construye las 15 escalas menores naturales en el pentagrama, grado a grado. Ejercicio interactivo gratuito para colocar las 8 notas siguiendo el patrón T-S-T-T-S-T-T.
- [Construir Escalas Menores Armónicas](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/escalas/construir-escala-menor-armonica/): Construye las escalas menores armónicas en el pentagrama: la menor natural con la 7ª elevada (sensible) y su 2ª aumentada característica. Ejercicio interactivo gratuito.
- [Construir Escalas Menores Melódicas](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/escalas/construir-escala-menor-melodica/): Construye la escala menor melódica completa en el pentagrama: sube con la 6ª y la 7ª elevadas y baja volviendo a la menor natural. Ejercicio interactivo gratuito de 15 notas.
- [Construir Escalas Dóricas](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/escalas/construir-escala-menor-dorica/): Construye las escalas dóricas en el pentagrama: la menor natural con la 6ª elevada. Ejercicio interactivo gratuito para colocar las 8 notas siguiendo el patrón T-S-T-T-T-S-T.
- [Ejercicios de Acordes Tríada](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/acordes/triadas/): Ejercicios de acordes tríada: tests para identificar y construir mayor, menor, disminuido y aumentado, y un generador de fichas con soluciones para imprimir.
- [Ejercicios de Acordes de Séptima](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/acordes/septimas/): Ejercicios de acordes de séptima: tests para identificar y construir la séptima de dominante, de sensible (semidisminuida) y disminuida, con sus cuatro posiciones.
- [Ejercicios de Articulación Musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/articulacion/): Test de articulación musical: legato, staccato, acento, tenuto y marcato. Da el nombre y adivina el signo en el pentagrama, o al revés. Gratis y online.
- [Ejercicios de Síncopas Online](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/compases/sincopa/): Ejercicio interactivo de síncopas: toca en el pentagrama la nota donde empieza la síncopa, o «no hay síncopa» si el ritmo no la tiene. Síncopa de tiempo, de parte y de compás. Gratis.
- [Ejercicios de Notas a Contratiempo Online](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/compases/contratiempo/): Ejercicio interactivo de notas a contratiempo: toca en el pentagrama la nota que está a contratiempo, o «no hay contratiempo» si el ritmo no la tiene. Contratiempo de parte y de tiempo. Gratis.
- [Ejercicio: el Puntillo es una Ligadura](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/figuras/puntillo-y-ligadura/): Ejercicio interactivo: toda figura con puntillo suena igual que una pareja de figuras ligadas. Reconoce la equivalencia en los dos sentidos, con puntillo simple y doble.
- [Equivalencias de Figuras Musicales](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/figuras/equivalencias-de-figuras/): Ejercicios de equivalencias entre figuras musicales: cuántas corcheas hay en una blanca con puntillo o qué figura equivale a tres negras. Con ficha PDF.
- [Ejercicios de Ligadura de Unión y de Expresión](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/figuras/ligaduras-de-union-y-expresion/): Ejercicio para distinguir la ligadura de unión de la de expresión y calcular cuánto dura la nota ligada en cada compás. Test online y ficha PDF.
- [Ejercicio: el Puntillo es una Ligadura](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/figuras/puntillo-y-ligadura/): Ejercicio interactivo: toda figura con puntillo suena igual que una pareja de figuras ligadas (con doble puntillo, un trío). Reconoce la equivalencia en los dos sentidos.
- [Escala Dórica](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/ejercicios/escalas/escalas-menores-dorica/): Ejercicios para identificar las escalas dóricas en el pentagrama: la escala menor con el 6º grado elevado. Test interactivo gratuito.

## Blog

- [Blog de Teoría Musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/blog/): Artículos sobre armonía, historia de la música y análisis musical.
- [Himno a San Juan (origen del solfeo)](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/blog/himno-a-san-juan/): Artículo sobre el origen de los nombres Do, Re, Mi, Fa, Sol, La, Si a partir del himno gregoriano Ut queant laxis.
- [Armonía](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/blog/armonia/): Introducción a la armonía tonal.
- [Práctica de Armonía nº 4a: Enlaces con Nota Común](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/blog/practica-no-4-a/): Ejercicio de armonía: realiza los enlaces guardando nota común e indica la tonalidad. Incluye audio de referencia y solución comentada paso a paso.
- [Práctica de Armonía nº 4b: Enlaces con Nota Común](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/blog/practica-no-4-b/): Ejercicio de armonía: realiza los enlaces guardando nota común e indica la tonalidad. Incluye audio de referencia y solución comentada paso a paso.
- [Práctica de Armonía nº 4c: Enlaces con Nota Común](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/blog/practica-no-4-c/): Ejercicio de armonía: realiza los enlaces guardando nota común e indica la tonalidad. Incluye audio de referencia y solución comentada paso a paso.
- [Práctica de Armonía nº 5a: Enlaces sin Nota Común](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/blog/practica-no-5-a/): Ejercicio de armonía: enlaces sin guardar nota común cuando el bajo procede por 3ª o 4ª ascendente o descendente. Con audio y solución comentada.
- [Práctica de Armonía nº 5b: Enlaces sin Nota Común](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/blog/practica-no-5-b/): Ejercicio de armonía: enlaces sin guardar nota común cuando el bajo procede por 3ª o 4ª. Práctica progresiva con audio de referencia y solución comentada.
- [Sobre mí: Eduardo Escrig Zomeño](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/sobre-mi/): Eduardo Escrig Zomeño, Titulado Superior en Musicología y profesor de lenguaje musical y percusión con más de 15 años de experiencia, autor de teoriamusical.com.es.
- [Cómo Usar el Metrónomo para Estudiar: Guía y Ejercicios](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/blog/como-usar-el-metronomo/): Aprende a estudiar con el metrónomo: el método de subir el tempo poco a poco y ejercicios en pentagrama (una escala con distintos ritmos y la pirámide de subdivisiones) para ganar precisión y técnica.
- [Cómo Leer el Cifrado de Acordes (C, Am, G7, Cmaj7…)](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/blog/como-leer-cifrado-de-acordes/): Aprende a leer el cifrado americano de acordes: las letras (A-G), mayor y menor, los números de séptima, sus2/sus4, los acordes con barra (C/G) y una tabla resumen.
- [Trucos para Memorizar las Escalas y las Armaduras](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/blog/trucos-memorizar-escalas-armaduras/): 5 trucos para aprenderte las armaduras de memoria: el orden de sostenidos y bemoles, sacar la tonalidad de un vistazo y el círculo de quintas como chuleta definitiva.
- [Cómo Calcular Intervalos Paso a Paso (con Ejemplos)](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/blog/como-calcular-intervalos-paso-a-paso/): Método en 2 pasos para calcular cualquier intervalo musical: cuenta el número y la cualidad (mayor, menor, justa…). Con tabla de semitonos y ejemplos resueltos.
- [Recursos Gratuitos para Estudiar Teoría Musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/blog/recursos-gratuitos-teoria-musical/): Libros, partituras de dominio público y programas realmente gratuitos, con su idioma, nivel y límites: Hutchinson (inglés), cuadernos de Néstor Crespo, método de solfeo de Eslava, musictheory.net, IMSLP y MuseScore Studio.
- [Agenda de Conciertos y Oposiciones de Música](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/agenda/): Agenda de conciertos de bandas y orquestas en España y oposiciones de música con el plazo abierto, comprobadas en fuentes oficiales.
- [Vallas musicales](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/entonacion/vallas/juego/)
- [Carrera de obstáculos musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/entonacion/carrera-de-obstaculos/juego/)
- [Salto de longitud musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/entonacion/salto-de-longitud/juego/)
- [Salto de altura musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/entonacion/salto-de-altura/juego/)
- [Lanzamiento de jabalina musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/entonacion/lanzamiento-de-jabalina/juego/)
- [Triple salto musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/entonacion/triple-salto/juego/)
- [100 metros lisos musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/entonacion/100-metros-lisos/juego/)
- [200 metros lisos musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/entonacion/200-metros-lisos/juego/)
- [400 metros lisos musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/entonacion/400-metros-lisos/juego/)
- [Juegos de Teoría Musical Online](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/): Juegos gratis para reconocer teoría musical a toda velocidad, sin micrófono: identifica intervalos, escalas y más, y pulsa la respuesta correcta antes de que se acabe el tiempo.
- [Dardos: juego para reconocer intervalos](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/dardos/): Juego gratis sin micrófono: aparece un intervalo escrito en el pentagrama y tienes que acertarlo antes de que se acabe el tiempo. Cuanto más rápido, más cerca del centro de la diana.
- [Dardos: reconoce intervalos](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/dardos/juego/)
- [Baloncesto: reconoce escalas](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/baloncesto/juego/)
- [Baloncesto: juego para reconocer escalas](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/baloncesto/): Juego gratis sin micrófono: aparece una escala completa escrita en el pentagrama, de ida y vuelta, y tienes que acertar su tónica y su tipo (mayor, menor natural, menor armónica o menor melódica) antes de que se acabe el tiempo. Elige tiro libre, de 2 o triple: cuanto más arriesgas, más puntos si aciertas. Se puede jugar solo o en grupo, por turnos, como en un partido.
- [Baloncesto: reconoce escalas](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/baloncesto/juego/)
- [Bolos: juego para reconocer acordes tríada](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/bolos/): Juego gratis sin micrófono: con la primera bola aciertas el estado del acorde tríada (fundamental, 1.ª o 2.ª inversión) y con la segunda su tipo (mayor, menor, aumentado o disminuido). Cada acierto derriba 5 bolos y las dos bien son pleno. Solo o en grupo, por turnos.
- [Bolos: reconoce acordes](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/bolos/juego/)
- [Fútbol: juego para construir intervalos](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/futbol/): Juego gratis sin micrófono: cada pase es un intervalo que escribes en el pentagrama desde la nota del que tiene el balón, y esa nota es la del compañero que lo recibe. Tres pases y un tiro por ataque; solo cuentan los goles. Solo o en grupo, con penaltis si hay empate.
- [Fútbol: construye intervalos](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/futbol/juego/)
- [Tiro al plato: juego para escribir escalas](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/tiro-al-plato/): Juego gratis sin micrófono: cada plato es una escala; primero dibujas su armadura y luego la escala, nota a nota. Si todo está bien, rompes el plato (1 punto). Mayores y menores natural, armónica y melódica. Solo o en grupo.
- [Tiro al plato: escribe escalas](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/tiro-al-plato/juego/)
- [Billar: juego para construir acordes tríada](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/billar/): Juego gratis sin micrófono: cada bola lleva un acorde tríada; eliges a cuál tirar y escribes sus notas en el pentagrama. Si está bien, la bola entra (1 punto); si no, se queda para volver a intentarlo. 5 bolas; en fundamental (Fácil), con 1.ª inversión (Medio) y con 2.ª (Difícil). Solo o en grupo.
- [Billar: construye acordes](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/teoria/billar/juego/)
- [Juegos auditivos](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/auditivos/): Juegos gratis para entrenar el oído musical, sin micrófono: escucha series de notas, recuérdalas y repítelas.
- [Memoriza: juego de memoria musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/auditivos/memoriza/): El tablero toca una serie de notas y la repites en el mismo orden; cada acierto añade una nota. Tres niveles: color y luz, solo luz y solo oído. Solo o en grupo, con una serie nueva para cada jugador.
- [Memoriza: memoria musical](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/auditivos/memoriza/juego/)
- [Ciclismo en pista: juego para reconocer mayor o menor de oído](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/auditivos/ciclismo-en-pista/): Juego auditivo gratis sin micrófono: el kilómetro en 4 vueltas; en cada una suena el La4 y una melodía de 8 compases y dices si está en modo mayor o menor. El reloj corre desde que empieza la melodía hasta que respondes (se puede desde el final del primer compás) y cada fallo suma 15 s. Gana el tiempo más bajo. Solo o en grupo.
- [Ciclismo en pista: mayor o menor](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/juegos/auditivos/ciclismo-en-pista/juego/)


## English edition

> The whole site is also available in English under https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/ (American English; British terms are marked "UK:"). Most English pages have a Spanish twin, linked with hreflang. Note names use letters (C D E F G A B) and the site follows the Spanish conservatory tradition where noted. Author: Eduardo Escrig Zomeño.

- [Home](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/)

### Free tools

- [Free Online Music Tools — Metronome & Tuner](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/): Free online music tools that run in your browser: a metronome with a drum machine, tap tempo and a speed trainer, and a chromatic tuner. No install, no sign-up.
- [Free Online Metronome — Drum Machine & Speed Trainer](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/metronome/): Free online metronome with simple, compound and custom time signatures (5/8, 7/8, 6/8…), a drum machine, tap tempo and a speed trainer. No install, works on your phone.
- [Free Online Chromatic Tuner — Guitar, Violin, Ukulele & More](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/): Free online chromatic tuner for guitar, bass, violin, ukulele, winds and more. Uses your microphone, shows cents and handles transposing instruments. No install, no sign-up.
- [Free Online Alto Saxophone Tuner — E♭ Transposing](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/alto-saxophone/): Tune your alto saxophone online with your microphone. E♭ transposing: shows the written and the sounding note. Adjustable A4. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Banjo Tuner — Open G and Other Tunings](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/banjo/): Tune your banjo with your microphone. Open G (gDGBD) for the 5-string banjo, plus 4-string tenor, plectrum and 6-string tunings. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Baritone Saxophone Tuner — E♭ Transposing](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/baritone-saxophone/): Tune your baritone saxophone online with your microphone. E♭ transposing: shows the written and the sounding note. Adjustable A4. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Bass Clarinet Tuner — B♭, Written Note](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/bass-clarinet/): Tune your bass clarinet online with your microphone. Shows the sounding note and the written note, with an adjustable A4 reference. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Bass Guitar Tuner — E A D G (4 and 5 Strings)](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/bass/): Tune your electric or acoustic bass online with your microphone. Standard E-A-D-G tuning for 4-string bass, plus tips for 5-string bass. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Bassoon Tuner — Concert Pitch, Adjustable A4](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/bassoon/): Tune your bassoon online with your microphone. A non-transposing instrument that reads from B♭1 up, fully inside the tuner’s range. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Cello Tuner — C G D A, Adjustable A4](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/cello/): Tune your cello with your microphone. Standard tuning in fifths C-G-D-A, an octave below the viola, with an adjustable A4 reference. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Clarinet Tuner — B♭ Clarinet, Written Note](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/clarinet/): Tune your B♭ clarinet online with your microphone. Shows the sounding note and the written note, with an adjustable A4 reference. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Contrabassoon Tuner — Sounds an Octave Lower](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/contrabassoon/): Tune your contrabassoon online with your microphone. It sounds an octave below written. Learn which low notes the tuner can read, and how to tune the rest.
- [Free Online Double Bass Tuner — E A D G, Low Notes](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/double-bass/): Tune your double bass with your microphone. Standard tuning in fourths E-A-D-G, plus how to tune the low C or B of a 5-string bass with a harmonic. Free.
- [Free Online E♭ Clarinet Tuner — Written Note (Requinto)](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/eb-clarinet/): Tune your E♭ clarinet (sopranino clarinet, “requinto”) online with your microphone. Shows the sounding and the written note. Free, no install.
- [Free Online English Horn Tuner — Transposing in F](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/english-horn/): Tune your English horn (UK: cor anglais) online with your microphone. It is in F and sounds a fifth below written; the tuner shows both. Free.
- [Free Online Euphonium Tuner — B♭, Bass or Treble Clef](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/euphonium/): Tune your euphonium online with your microphone. Shows sounding and written notes for bass clef or treble clef parts, A4 adjustable. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Flugelhorn Tuner — B♭ Transposing](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/flugelhorn/): Tune your flugelhorn online with your microphone. Shows the sounding and the written note for a B♭ flugelhorn, A4 adjustable. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Flute Tuner — Concert Pitch, Adjustable A4](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/flute/): Tune your concert flute online with your microphone. A non-transposing instrument in C, with adjustable A4 (440 Hz standard). Free, no install.
- [Free Online French Horn Tuner — Horn in F](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/french-horn/): Tune your French horn online with your microphone. Shows the sounding and written note for a horn in F, A4 adjustable. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Guitar Tuner — Standard E A D G B E](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/guitar/): Tune your acoustic, electric or classical guitar online with your microphone. Standard tuning E-A-D-G-B-E and any alternate tuning. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Harp Tuner — Pedal and Lever Harps](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/harp/): Tune your harp with your microphone. Reads the sounding note at concert pitch, with an adjustable A4. Pedal harps are tuned in natural. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Mandolin Tuner — G D A E, Paired Strings](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/mandolin/): Tune your mandolin with your microphone. Standard tuning G-D-A-E in fifths, same as the violin, with 8 strings in 4 pairs, plus how to tune it by ear. Free.
- [Free Online Oboe Tuner — Concert Pitch, Adjustable A4](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/oboe/): Tune your oboe online with your microphone. A non-transposing instrument, and the one that gives the orchestra its A. A4 adjustable. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Piccolo Tuner — Sounds an Octave Higher](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/piccolo/): Tune your piccolo online with your microphone. It sounds an octave above the written note, and the tuner shows both. A4 adjustable. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Saxophone Tuner — Alto, Tenor, Soprano, Bari](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/saxophone/): Tune your saxophone online with your microphone. Written note to play for concert A on soprano, alto, tenor and baritone sax. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Soprano Saxophone Tuner — B♭ Transposing](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/soprano-saxophone/): Tune your soprano saxophone online with your microphone. B♭ transposing: shows the written and the sounding note. Adjustable A4. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Tenor Saxophone Tuner — B♭ Transposing](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/tenor-saxophone/): Tune your tenor saxophone online with your microphone. B♭ transposing: shows the written and the sounding note. Adjustable A4. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Timpani Tuner — Pedal Tuning and Ranges](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/timpani/): Tune your orchestral timpani online with your microphone. Pitch ranges of the 32, 29, 26 and 23 inch drums, and how to read a drum’s pitch. Free.
- [Free Online Trombone Tuner — Tenor and Bass Trombone](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/trombone/): Tune your tenor or bass trombone online with your microphone. Concert pitch, slide positions and tuning slide tips, A4 adjustable. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Trumpet Tuner — B♭ Transposing](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/trumpet/): Tune your trumpet online with your microphone. Shows the sounding and the written note for a B♭ trumpet, A4 adjustable. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Tuba Tuner — BB♭, CC, E♭ and F Tubas](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/tuba/): Tune your tuba online with your microphone. Concert pitch for BB♭, CC, E♭ and F tubas, with tips for the lowest notes. A4 adjustable. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Ukulele Tuner — G C E A (Soprano, Concert, Tenor)](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/ukulele/): Tune your ukulele online for free with your microphone. G-C-E-A tuning for soprano, concert and tenor, and D-G-B-E for baritone. No install.
- [Free Online Viola Tuner — C G D A, Adjustable A4](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/viola/): Tune your viola with your microphone. Standard tuning in fifths C-G-D-A, a fifth below the violin, with an adjustable A4 reference. Free, no install.
- [Free Online Violin Tuner — G D A E, Adjustable A4](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/tools/tuner/violin/): Tune your violin with your microphone. Standard tuning in fifths G-D-A-E, with an adjustable A4 reference (440 Hz standard, 442 Hz in many orchestras). Free.

### Music dictionary

- [Music Theory Dictionary: Concepts Explained Clearly](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/): Music theory dictionary: intervals, chords, time signatures, scales, keys and clefs. Clear explanations with staff examples, audio and exercises. Free.
- [Accidentals in Music: Sharp, Flat, Natural and Double](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/accidentals/): Accidentals raise or lower a note: sharp, flat, natural, double sharp and double flat. Learn what each does and how long an accidental lasts in a measure.
- [Agogics: Tempo Changes (rit., accel., a tempo, fermata)](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/agogics/): What agogics are and what accelerando, ritardando, rallentando, ritenuto, a tempo, più mosso, rubato and the fermata mean, and how they differ.
- [Articulation in Music: Legato, Staccato, Accent, Tenuto](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/articulation/): Musical articulation: how each note is attacked and joined. Legato, staccato, accent, tenuto and marcato, with their symbols, effect and staff examples.
- [Musical Cadences: Authentic, Plagal, Half and Deceptive](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/cadences/): The types of cadence: authentic (perfect, imperfect), plagal, half and deceptive. Chords of each, US and UK names, and C major staff examples with audio.
- [Musical Chords: Types, Formation and Function](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/chords/): Musical chords explained: triads (major, minor, augmented, diminished) and seventh chords. How they are built, their symbols and their harmonic function.
- [Augmented Chord: What It Is, How to Build It and Symbol](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/chords/augmented-triad/): The augmented chord is a triad with a major 3rd and an augmented 5th (C–E–G♯). How to build it, its symbol (C+, Caug) and where it appears.
- [Diminished Seventh Chord (dim7): Formation and Use](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/chords/diminished-seventh-chord/): The diminished seventh chord is three stacked minor thirds on the leading tone of a minor key. Formation, enharmonic spellings, inversions and use.
- [Diminished Chord: What It Is, How to Build It and Symbol](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/chords/diminished-triad/): The diminished chord is a triad with a minor 3rd and a diminished 5th (C–E♭–G♭). How to build it, its symbol (C°, Cdim) and how it differs from a dim7.
- [Dominant Seventh Chord (V7): What It Is and Resolution](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/chords/dominant-seventh-chord/): The dominant seventh chord (V7) has a major 3rd, perfect 5th and minor 7th on degree V. Notes, inversions, figured bass and how it resolves to the tonic.
- [Half-Diminished Seventh Chord (Leading-Tone Seventh)](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/chords/leading-tone-seventh-chord/): The half-diminished (leading-tone) seventh chord on degree vii of a major key: notes, intervals, inversions and figured bass, and how it resolves.
- [Major Seventh Chord (Cmaj7): What It Is and How to Build It](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/chords/major-seventh-chord/): The major seventh chord (Cmaj7) is a major triad plus a major 7th: C–E–G–B. How it is built, its symbols, its bright sound and where it appears.
- [Major Chord (Major Triad): How to Build It and Symbol](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/chords/major-triad/): The major chord is a triad with a major 3rd and a perfect 5th (C–E–G), with a bright sound. How it is built, its symbol and the degrees where it appears.
- [Minor Seventh Chord (Cm7): What It Is and How to Build It](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/chords/minor-seventh-chord/): The minor seventh chord (Cm7) is a minor triad plus a minor 7th: C–E♭–G–B♭. How it is built, its symbols, its sound and the scale degrees where it appears.
- [Minor Triad (Minor Chord): Notes, Formula and Symbol](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/chords/minor-triad/): The minor triad is a minor 3rd plus a perfect 5th, with a darker sound. How it is built (C–E♭–G), how it is written (Cm) and where it falls in the scale.
- [Seventh Chords: The 5 Types, Symbols and Structure](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/chords/seventh-chords/): Seventh chords explained: the 5 types (dominant, major, minor, half-diminished, diminished), their structure and symbols (C7, Cmaj7, Cm7…).
- [Triads: The 4 Types, Inversions and Figured Bass](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/chords/triads/): Triads explained: major, minor, augmented and diminished, their inversions, the triads of the major and natural minor scales and figured bass.
- [Musical Clefs: Treble, Bass and C Clef Explained](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/clefs/): What clefs are: the treble, bass and C clefs show which note sits on each line of the staff. Which clef each instrument reads, with a comparison chart.
- [Bass Clef: What It Is, Notes and How to Read It](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/clefs/bass-clef/): The bass clef (F clef) puts F3 on the 4th line of the staff. Learn all its notes, a memory trick, ledger lines and the instruments that read it.

- [Types of Musical Scales: Every Scale Explained](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/keys-and-scales/types-of-scales/): All the types of musical scales: major, minor, modes, pentatonic, blues, chromatic, whole-tone and color scales. What each one is and how it is built.
- [Whole-Tone Scale: Notes, Sound and Examples](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/keys-and-scales/whole-tone-scale/): The whole-tone scale: 6 notes a whole step apart. Why only two exist, its ambiguous floating sound and its use by Debussy and the Impressionists.
- [Modulation in Music: What It Is, Types and Examples](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/modulation/): What modulation is and how it works: diatonic (pivot chord), chromatic and enharmonic modulation, neighboring keys, with notation and audio examples.
- [Musical Phrase: Motive, Phrase and Period Explained](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/musical-phrase/): What a musical phrase is and how music is organized: motive, sub-phrase, phrase and period, with a language analogy and a diagram of an 8-measure period.
- [Phrase Beginnings: Downbeat, Pickup and Off-Beat Starts](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/musical-phrase/phrase-beginnings/): The three ways a phrase can begin: on the downbeat (thetic), with a pickup or anacrusis, or after a rest (acephalous). Staff examples and well-known songs.
- [Phrase Endings: Strong Beat vs Weak Beat](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/musical-phrase/phrase-endings/): How a phrase ends: on a strong beat (masculine ending) or a weak beat (feminine ending). Staff examples, how to tell them apart, and cadence vs ending.
- [Note Names: Letters, Do-Re-Mi and German H Explained](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/note-names/): The 7 musical notes and their names in letters (C-B), fixed-do solfège (Do-Si) and German (C-H). Full equivalence tables and note positions in every clef.
- [Note Values and Rests: Names, Durations and Chart](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/note-values/): The 7 note values (whole, half, quarter, eighth, sixteenth…), their duration in beats, equivalences and matching rests, with a chart and symbols.
- [Octave Numbers: Scientific Pitch vs Franco-Belgian](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/octave-numbering/): Octave numbers name the exact C, A or F you mean. Compare scientific pitch notation (middle C = C4) with the Franco-Belgian system (C3), with a chart.
- [Musical Ornaments: Trill, Mordent, Turn, Appoggiatura](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/ornaments/): Musical ornaments explained: appoggiatura, acciaccatura, mordent, turn and trill. How each is written and played, with examples you can listen to.
- [Performance Effects: Glissando, Vibrato, Tremolo](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/performance-effects/): Performance effects in music: glissando, portamento, arpeggiato, vibrato and tremolo. What each does, how it is marked, and how it differs from ornaments.
- [Arpeggiated (Rolled) Chord: Meaning and Notation](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/performance-effects/arpeggiated-chord/): What an arpeggiated or rolled chord is, how the wavy line is written, and how it differs from an arpeggio. Notation examples and audio.
- [Glissando: Meaning, Notation and Examples](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/performance-effects/glissando/): What a glissando is: a slide between two notes. How it is written, continuous vs. stepped types, glissando vs. portamento, famous examples and audio.
- [Portamento in Music: Meaning and Glissando Difference](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/performance-effects/portamento/): What portamento is: an expressive slide from one note to the next. How it sounds, how it differs from glissando and portato, and which instruments use it.
- [Tremolo in Music: Meaning, Notation and Vibrato Difference](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/performance-effects/tremolo/): What tremolo is, how it is written with slashes on the stem, and how it differs from vibrato and the trill. Notation examples and audio.
- [Vibrato in Music: What It Is and How It Is Played](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/performance-effects/vibrato/): What vibrato is: a regular oscillation of pitch. Speed and width, how each instrument does it, and how it differs from tremolo and the trill. With audio.
- [Qualities of Sound: Pitch, Duration, Intensity, Timbre](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/qualities-of-sound/): The four qualities of musical sound: pitch (high/low), duration, intensity (loud/soft) and timbre. What each is, what it depends on and how it is written.
- [Repeat Signs in Music: D.C., D.S., Coda, Endings](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/repeat-signs/): Learn musical repeat signs: repeat barlines, first and second endings, Da Capo, Dal Segno, Coda and Fine, with examples and interactive audio.

- [Tempo in Music: Largo, Andante, Allegro and BPM Chart](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/tempo/): What tempo is in music, the Italian tempo markings from slowest to fastest (Largo to Presto) with their BPM, and tempo changes (rit., accel., a tempo).
- [Tie vs Slur in Music: Differences and Examples](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/ties-and-slurs/): A tie joins notes of the same pitch and adds their duration; a slur (legato) joins different pitches. Learn the difference, with examples and a quick rule.
- [Time Signatures: Simple and Compound Meter Explained](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/): What a time signature and a measure are, how simple and compound meters differ, and how to read the numbers. Examples in 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8.
- [12/8 Time Signature: What It Is, How to Count It, Examples](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/12-8-time/): 12/8 is a compound meter counted in four dotted-quarter-note beats. The time signature of slow blues and ballads, with staff examples and audio.
- [2/4 Time Signature: How to Count It, With Examples](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/2-4-time/): 2/4 is a simple meter with two quarter-note beats per measure. Learn how to count it, how it differs from 6/8 and 4/4, and hear a melody in 2/4.
- [3/2 Time Signature: Meaning, Counting and Examples](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/3-2-time/): 3/2 is a simple meter with three half-note beats per measure. Learn how to count it, how it differs from 3/4 and 6/4, and hear a melody in 3/2.
- [3/4 Time Signature: The Waltz Meter, With Examples](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/3-4-time/): 3/4 is a simple meter with three quarter-note beats per measure, the waltz meter. Learn how to count it, how it differs from 6/8, and hear an example.
- [3/8 Time Signature: Simple or Compound? Examples](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/3-8-time/): 3/8 is a simple meter with three eighth-note beats per measure. Find out why it is not compound, how to count it, and hear a melody in 3/8.
- [4/4 Time Signature (Common Time): How to Count It](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/4-4-time/): 4/4, or common time (C), is a simple meter with four quarter-note beats per measure, the most used meter in music. Learn how to count it, with examples.
- [6/4 Time Signature: Meaning, Counting and Hemiola](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/6-4-time/): 6/4 is a compound meter with two dotted-half-note beats per measure. Learn how to count it, how it differs from 6/8 and 3/2, and what a hemiola is.
- [6/8 Time Signature: How to Count It, With Examples](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/6-8-time/): 6/8 is a compound meter with two dotted-quarter-note beats per measure. Learn how to count it, why it is felt in two, and how it differs from 3/4.
- [9/8 Time Signature: How to Count It, With Examples](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/9-8-time/): 9/8 is a compound meter with three dotted-quarter-note beats per measure. Learn how to count it, how it differs from 3/4, and hear a melody in 9/8.
- [Accents in Compound Meter: Beats in 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/accents-in-compound-meters/): Strong and weak beats in compound meter: 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8. Why 6/8 is not 3/4, and how compound meters differ from simple ones.
- [Accents in Simple Meter: Beats in 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/accents-in-simple-meters/): Strong and weak beats in simple meter: 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4. The waltz pattern S-W-W and the 4/4 pattern S-W-M-W explained with staff examples.
- [How to Analyze Time Signatures: A Practical Guide](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/analyzing-time-signatures/): How to read a time signature: the top number gives the beats and the bottom number the note value. Tell simple from compound meter step by step.
- [Beat Unit and Measure Unit: What They Are, With Examples](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/beat-unit-and-measure-unit/): The beat unit is the note value of one beat; the measure unit is the note value that fills a whole measure. Learn how to read time signature numbers.
- [Cut Time (Alla Breve, 2/2): Meaning and How to Count](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/cut-time/): Cut time, or alla breve (¢), equals 2/2: two half-note beats per measure. Learn what the symbol means, how it differs from common time, and hear it.
- [Off-Beat Notes: What They Are and How to Write Them](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/off-beat-notes/): An off-beat note starts on a weak beat or weak part of a beat, right after a rest. Definition, staff examples and how it differs from syncopation.
- [Pickup Notes (Anacrusis): What It Is and How to Write It](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/pickup-anacrusis/): What a pickup (anacrusis, upbeat) is, how it is written on the staff and how the last measure is completed. With examples such as Happy Birthday.
- [Simple vs Compound Meter: Differences and Examples](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/simple-and-compound-meter/): Simple meter divides each beat into two, compound meter into three. Learn to tell them apart by the top number and the beat unit, with a chart of examples.
- [Syncopation in Music: Types, Examples and Notation](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/time-signatures/syncopation/): Syncopation shifts the accent: a note starts on a weak beat and sounds through the next strong one. Types, staff examples and the off-beat difference.
- [Tuplets in Music: Triplets, Duplets, Quintuplets](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/tuplets/): What tuplets are: triplet, duplet, quadruplet, quintuplet, sextuplet and septuplet. How they are written and how long they last, with examples.
- [Duplet in Music: What It Is and How to Count It](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/tuplets/duplet/): A duplet puts two notes in the time of three, typical of compound meters like 6/8. How to count it, its types and why it is the opposite of the triplet.
- [Triplets in Music: What They Are and How to Count Them](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/music-dictionary/tuplets/triplet/): A triplet fits three equal notes into the time of two. Learn how to write and count triplets, the main types, and how a triplet differs from 6/8.

- [Note Values in Each Time Signature: Beats Quiz](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/exercises/rhythm/note-values/note-value-in-each-time-signature/): Quiz on how many beats each note and rest lasts in 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8, with dots and double dots. Instant answers, no sign-up.
- [Tie or Slur? Free Online Exercise With Answers](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/exercises/rhythm/note-values/ties-and-slurs/): Exercise to tell a tie from a slur and work out how long the tied note lasts in each time signature. Instant answers, no sign-up.
- [Phrase Beginnings: Downbeat, Pickup or Off-Beat Start](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/exercises/rhythm/phrase-beginnings/): Exercise: tell whether a melody starts on the downbeat, on a pickup (anacrusis) or after a rest, from its first two measures. Three levels, worksheets.
- [Phrase Endings: Strong Beat or Weak Beat Exercise](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/exercises/rhythm/phrase-endings/): Exercise: tell whether a melody ends on a strong beat (masculine) or a weak beat (feminine) from its last two measures. Three levels, worksheets.
- [Time Signature Exercises: Free Online Quizzes](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/exercises/rhythm/time-signatures/): Time signature exercises: analyze a time signature, complete measures with a missing note, recognize the time signature from rhythm, find syncopation.
- [Time Signature Analysis Quiz: Simple or Compound?](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/exercises/rhythm/time-signatures/analyze-time-signatures/): Practice analyzing time signatures: simple or compound, number of beats, subdivision and beat, subdivision and measure units. Free online quiz.
- [Complete the Measure: Missing Note or Rest Quiz](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/exercises/rhythm/time-signatures/complete-the-measure/): Find the missing note or rest in a measure of 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8, 9/8 or 12/8. Three levels, instant feedback, and a worksheet generator with solutions.
- [Off-Beat Notes Exercises Online: Find the Off-Beat](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/exercises/rhythm/time-signatures/off-beat-notes/): Free off-beat exercise: tap the note that is off the beat, or "no off-beat". Off-beat on a half beat and on a whole beat. Worksheets.
- [Recognize the Time Signature: Quiz With Answers](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/exercises/rhythm/time-signatures/recognize-time-signature/): Work out the time signature (2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8, 9/8, 12/8) from the written rhythm. Instant feedback, worksheet generator and explanations.
- [Syncopation Exercises Online: Find the Syncopation](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/exercises/rhythm/time-signatures/syncopation/): Free syncopation exercise: tap the note where the syncopation starts, or "no syncopation". Beat, half-beat and measure syncopation. Worksheets.
- [Which Time Signature? Quiz With Triplets and Tuplets](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/exercises/rhythm/time-signatures/which-time-signature/): Name the time signature of a measure filled with triplets, duplets, quadruplets and sextuplets by simplifying each tuplet. Three levels, worksheets.

### Music games

- [Free Online Music Games: Singing, Theory and Ear Training](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/): Free music games in your browser: sing in tune with your microphone, read scales, intervals and chords on the staff, or train your ear. No sign-up.
- [Ear Training Games Online: Free Musical Ear Practice](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/ear-training/): Free ear training games, no microphone: repeat longer and longer note sequences, or say whether a melody is major or minor against the clock.
- [Memorize: Free Musical Memory Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/ear-training/memorize/): Free ear training game: listen to a sequence of notes and repeat it on the board. It grows by one note each time. Three levels, from colors to ear only.
- [Track Cycling: Major or Minor Ear Training Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/ear-training/track-cycling/): Free ear training game: race the kilometer by saying whether each piano melody is major or minor. The clock runs until you answer; a mistake adds 15 s.
- [Singing Games Online: Free Pitch and Ear Training](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/singing/): Free singing games to train your pitch: sing a note, interval, chord or scale and the microphone checks if you are in tune. Nine games, no install.
- [100-Meter Dash: Free Melody Singing Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/singing/100-metres-dash/): Free ear-training game: sing a short melody from memory, note by note. You only move on when you hit each pitch. Run the 100-meter dash with your voice.
- [200-Meter Dash: Free Long Melody Singing Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/singing/200-metres-dash/): Free ear-training game: sing a long melody of two phrases from memory, note by note. You only move on when you hit each pitch. Run the 200-meter dash.
- [400-Meter Dash: Free Very Long Melody Singing Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/singing/400-metres-dash/): Free ear-training game: sing a very long melody of four phrases from memory, note by note. Move on only when you hit each pitch. Run the 400-meter dash.
- [High Jump: Free Interval Singing Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/singing/high-jump/): Free ear-training game: sing two notes, the first is the run and the second the jump. Three difficulties and the intervals you choose, from 2nds to 7ths.
- [110-Meter Hurdles: Free Scale Singing Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/singing/hurdles/): Free ear-training game: sing a major or minor scale note by note. Each note is a hurdle you clear only when it is in tune. Run the 110-meter hurdles.
- [Javelin Throw: Free Glissando Singing Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/singing/javelin-throw/): Free ear-training game: sing a glissando between two notes and throw the javelin. Stay inside the lane to make it fly farther. Uses your microphone.
- [Long Jump: Free Note Singing Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/singing/long-jump/): Free ear-training game: listen to a note, sing it for 5 seconds and jump farther the more in tune you are. Works with your phone or computer microphone.
- [Obstacle Race: Interval Singing Game (Steeplechase)](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/singing/obstacle-race/): Free singing game inspired by the steeplechase (3000 m obstacle race): sing 8 intervals in a row from a base note. You clear each one only when in tune.
- [Triple Jump: Free Chord Arpeggio Singing Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/singing/triple-jump/): Free ear-training game: hear a major or minor chord and sing its arpeggio (root, third and fifth). Each note you tune adds meters to your triple jump.
- [Music Theory Games Online: Intervals, Scales, Chords](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/theory/): Free music theory games, no microphone: recognize intervals, scales and chords on the staff, or write them yourself. Solo or in class, with a leaderboard.
- [Basketball: Free Scale Recognition Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/theory/basketball/): Free music theory game, no microphone: name the full scale on the staff before time runs out. Choose a free throw, a 2-pointer or a three-pointer.
- [Billiards: Free Triad-Building Music Theory Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/theory/billiards/): Free music theory game, no microphone: pick a ball, write its triad on the staff, and sink it if the chord is right. Solo or in class.
- [Bowling: Free Triad Chord Recognition Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/theory/bowling/): Free music theory game, no microphone: name each triad’s position and type to knock down pins. Play solo or in turns, and chain strikes for a top score.
- [Clay Target Shooting: Free Scale-Writing Music Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/theory/clay-shooting/): Free music theory game, no microphone: write the key signature and then the scale to break each clay target. Major and minor, any key. Solo or in class.
- [Darts: Free Interval Recognition Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/theory/darts/): Free music theory game: read the two notes on the staff and pick the interval. The faster you answer, the closer your dart lands to the bullseye.
- [Soccer: Free Interval-Building Music Theory Game](https://www.teoriamusical.com.es/en/games/theory/soccer/): Free music theory game, no microphone: each pass is an interval you write on the staff, and the passes chain into a goal. Solo or in class.
